title: Edge anti-spam agents are enabled
description: The Edge Transport server MUST have content filtering, recipient filtering, sender filtering, and connection filtering agents enabled. The Connection Filtering agent is enabled or disabled independently via Enable-TransportAgent / Disable-TransportAgent, not via a *-ConnectionFilterConfig cmdlet. Disabled anti-spam agents allow spam, phishing, and malicious mail to pass to internal mail servers without inspection.
subject: Server

references.name: Microsoft — Antispam protection in Exchange Server
DISA STIG EX19-ED-000102: The Exchange content filter must be enabled (V-259626)
DISA STIG EX19-ED-000104: The Exchange Recipient Filter must be enabled (V-259627)
DISA STIG EX19-ED-000106: The Exchange Sender Filter must be enabled (V-259628)

remediation.description: Enable the relevant agent(s). For content, recipient, and sender filtering use Set-ContentFilterConfig -Enabled $true, Set-RecipientFilterConfig -Enabled $true, or Set-SenderFilterConfig -Enabled $true. For connection filtering, enable the Connection Filtering transport agent with Enable-TransportAgent 'Connection Filtering Agent' then restart the transport service.
remediation.scriptTemplate:
Get-ContentFilterConfig | Select-Object Enabled
Get-RecipientFilterConfig | Select-Object Enabled
Get-SenderFilterConfig | Select-Object Enabled
Get-TransportAgent -Identity 'Connection Filtering Agent' | Select-Object Identity,Enabled
# To enable connection filtering:
# Enable-TransportAgent 'Connection Filtering Agent'
# Restart-Service MSExchangeTransport

considerations: Enabling or tuning anti-spam agents may temporarily affect mail flow if the thresholds are misconfigured. Test in a staging environment when possible.
